title: Year 11 Biology Module 1 – Cells as the Basis of Life
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 11 Biology Module 1. Questions are designed for short answers with no multi-step calculations or extended writing.
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

questions.prompt: What is the basic structural and functional unit of life?
Which type of cell lacks a membrane-bound nucleus?
Which type of cell contains membrane-bound organelles?
What rigid outer structure is found in plant cells and most bacterial cells?
What region of a bacterial cell contains its main circular DNA?
Which organelle contains most of a eukaryotic cell's DNA?
Which organelle is the main site of aerobic cellular respiration?
Which tiny structures are the site of protein synthesis?
Which organelle modifies, sorts and packages proteins?
Which organelle carries out photosynthesis in plant cells?
What term means how many times larger an image is than the object?
Which microscope can be used to observe living cells?
Which electron microscope shows internal ultrastructure in thin sections?
questions.answer: A transmission electron microscope. Accept: TEM.

questions.prompt: Which electron microscope gives detailed images of a cell's surface?
questions.answer: A scanning electron microscope. Accept: SEM.

questions.prompt: What term describes how well a microscope can distinguish two close points?
What model describes the cell membrane as a moving phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins?
What is movement of particles from high to low concentration called?
What is movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane called?
What transport process uses energy to move substances against a concentration gradient?
Name the two vesicle-based processes that move large materials into and out of cells.
What gas is taken in for photosynthesis?
What gas is released during photosynthesis?
What process releases usable energy from glucose in cells?
What name is given to biological catalysts that speed up cellular reactions?
What is the name of the region on an enzyme where the substrate binds?

finalRound.prompt: As a cell gets larger, which ratio decreases and can limit efficient exchange across the membrane?
finalRound.answer: The surface-area-to-volume ratio. Accept: SA:V ratio.
